subsystems.name: Seed factory
subsystems.role: the smallest set of machines that can build copies of itself and then build the structure.

subsystems.name: Feedstock system
subsystems.role: acquires and refines raw material — asteroid rock, lunar regolith or scrap — into usable stock.

subsystems.name: Fabrication units
subsystems.role: turn refined material into parts: trusses, panels, tanks, cables.

subsystems.name: Assembly robots
subsystems.role: join parts into bigger parts, and parts into structure.

subsystems.name: Structure
subsystems.role: the megastructure itself, grown incrementally rather than launched whole.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: runs the factory and rejects the heat, at whatever scale the structure has reached.

subsystems.name: Control and verification
subsystems.role: keeps the swarm coordinated, safe and self-repairing without humans nearby.

buildSteps.title: Define the seed
buildSteps.detail: Engineers work out the minimum set of machines whose combined output can build another copy of that same set — the theoretical self-replicating 'seed'.

buildSteps.title: Deliver the seed
buildSteps.detail: Launch the seed to a feedstock-rich site: a near-Earth asteroid, or the lunar surface where regolith is already loose and abundant.

buildSteps.title: Mine and refine
buildSteps.detail: Robots dig or scoop material and process it in vacuum: grind, separate, reduce oxides, and produce metal powder, wire and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate components
buildSteps.detail: Printers and formers turn feedstock into standard parts — tubes, panels, brackets, tanks — designed so the same few shapes assemble into many things.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a copy
buildSteps.detail: The robots build a second seed factory from the parts, closing the replication loop under its own control. This is the step no machine has yet performed.

buildSteps.title: Grow the structure
buildSteps.detail: With replication proven, copy count rises; the growing fleet assembles ever-larger trusses and shells rather than shipping modules from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Scale power and cooling
buildSteps.detail: Power supply and radiators are extended in step with the structure, since waste heat is the hard limit on how much work can be done.

buildSteps.title: Verify and repair
buildSteps.detail: Continuous inspection finds failed joints or parts, and repair robots replace them — a megastructure must be maintainable, not just buildable.

buildSteps.title: Outfit and commission
buildSteps.detail: Habitat sections are sealed, pressurised, shielded and fitted with life support before people or equipment move in.

prerequisites.why: supervised robots work in orbit today, but self-replication needs machines that decide and repair without a human in the loop.
additive manufacturing has been demonstrated on the International Space Station, but only at kilogram scale.

prerequisites.tech: Closed-loop material refining in vacuum and microgravity
prerequisites.why: melting, separating and casting rock and metal off Earth has never been done at industrial scale.
self-replicating probes are a theoretical construction; no machine has yet built a copy of itself from local material.
'molecular assemblers' are a hypothesis about future chemistry, not a demonstrated process.

prerequisites.tech: Megawatt-to-gigawatt power and heat rejection in space
prerequisites.why: solar arrays exist, but radiating industrial-scale waste heat away in vacuum requires very large radiator area.

pathway.milestone: In-space additive manufacturing and robotic servicing at kilogram scale
pathway.unlocks: confidence that useful parts and repairs need not come from Earth.

pathway.milestone: Robotic extraction and refining of lunar or asteroid material
pathway.unlocks: feedstock that costs nothing to launch, removing the dominant mass penalty.

pathway.milestone: A demonstrator that builds most of its own subsystems from local material
pathway.unlocks: exponential growth of industrial capacity instead of linear growth.

pathway.milestone: Kilometre-scale structures assembled in orbit, such as habitats or solar power satellites
pathway.unlocks: large habitable volume and continuous solar energy, per concepts studied from the 1970s onward.
continent-scale infrastructure — only if materials, control and power all reach levels not yet in sight.
